learning_objective: 🎯 Discover how your brain acts as a supercomputer and how chemical hormones send messages to control every action in plants and animals!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The nervous system uses electrical impulses to send fast messages. The structural unit is the Neuron (dendrites receive signals, axon passes them). The gap between two neurons is a 'Synapse', where chemicals transmit the signal.

A reflex is a sudden, involuntary response to a dangerous stimulus (like touching a hot pan). The signal travels to the spinal cord and bounces back instantly to the muscles without waiting for the brain to think. This path is the Reflex Arc.

Divided into Forebrain (thinking, memory), Midbrain, and Hindbrain (involuntary actions). The Cerebellum (part of hindbrain) controls balance and posture, while the Medulla controls heartbeat and breathing.

Plants don't have brains, but they respond to stimuli by growing. Phototropism (bending towards light), Geotropism (roots growing towards gravity), and Hydrotropism (roots growing towards water) are controlled by plant hormones like Auxin.

Glands secrete chemicals called Hormones directly into the blood for slow but long-lasting effects. Adrenaline prepares the body for 'fight or flight', Insulin regulates blood sugar, and Thyroxine regulates metabolism.

fun_activity.title: 📏 The Ruler Drop Reflex
fun_activity.instructions: Have a friend hold a 30cm ruler vertically above your open hand. They drop it without warning, and you must catch it as fast as possible. The measurement where you catch it shows how fast your nervous system reacts!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly differentiate between Voluntary (walking), Involuntary (heartbeat), and Reflex actions (blinking/pulling hand away).
📌 Learn the functions of specific plant hormones: Auxin (growth), Gibberellins (stem growth), Cytokinins (cell division), Abscisic acid (wilting/stopping growth).
📌 Iodine is necessary for the thyroid gland to make thyroxine; deficiency causes Goitre.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Central Nervous System (CNS) consists of the brain and spinal cord.
⭐ Electrical signals in a neuron travel from Dendrite → Cell Body → Axon → Nerve ending.
⭐ Hormones act as chemical messengers to coordinate growth, development, and responses to the environment.
